## Must-Fix 1 — missing 5th surface: `lens-coverage-map.md` (ADDRESSED)

`workflow_lint.py::check_lens_coverage` runs in the **no-flags default** dispatch
(line 18560) and FAILs for any LESSONS.md rule name lacking a coverage-map row
(`LESSONS.md rule '<rule>' has no coverage row in the map`, line 15580). Every one
of the 52 existing rules has such a row. As specced at v2 the change would have
FAILed its own acceptance criterion 4 ("no-flags workflow_lint clean") — while the
plan's own must-stop clause ("editing any 5th file") forbade the only remedy. A
self-defeating spec, the #488 plan-contradiction class at small scale.

**Verified independently before revising** (not taken on the critic's word): read
the no-flags dispatch line, the FAIL text, the 52-row table, and
`_LENS_STATE_PREFIXES = ("v2-owner:", "v1-only", "retired:", "GAP:")`.

**Fix in v3:** added file 5 — one `lens-coverage-map.md` row in the same
alphabetical position, `| blinded-reads | LESSONS.md | v2-owner: orchestrator
(blinded-read dispatch discipline; workflow-version-independent) |` (the
`context-hygiene` shape: orchestrator-owned and workflow-version-independent
rather than owned by a v2 critic). File count 4 → 5 in the diffs section and the
Reproducibility Card; must-stop clause amended to "any 6th file"; new success
criterion 3b pins `--check-lens-coverage` → PASS.

## Should-Fix 1 — § Ordering incomplete, and its diagnostic misleading (ADDRESSED)

The guard runs the FULL parity check at edit time, so a LESSONS row naming a
not-yet-created rule file is blocked too (the guard's own self-test case 4). The
v2 constraint ("bump the constant before the LESSONS edit") was necessary but not
sufficient, and its diagnostic sentence — "if the guard blocks, the constant bump
is missing or wrong" — would have misdirected an implementer who bumped the
constant but had not yet written `blinded-reads.md`.

**Fix in v3:** ordering restated as **files 1 AND 3 both before file 2**, with the
two preconditions named explicitly, and the diagnostic rewritten to tell the two
block causes apart by the guard's own surfaced lint text (a byte-cap message ⇒ the
constant; a parity / `has no matching rule file` message ⇒ file 1 absent). The
no-escape-hatch instruction is retained and unweakened.

## Should-Fix 2 — name the lint-recognized waiver token (ADDRESSED)

`API_DISPATCH_ROUTING_EXEMPT` is not an ad-hoc comment: it is a lint-recognized
waiver (`workflow_lint.py::API_DISPATCH_ROUTING_WAIVER`, line 15362, checked in
the no-flags default). A future blinded-read script following this rule would trip
the non-dispatcher-caller check unless it carries the literal token.

**Fix in v3:** the rule's *Not the dispatcher* section now specifies the literal
`# API_DISPATCH_ROUTING_EXEMPT: <reason>` token and notes it is a sanctioned
exemption class, so rule-compliant blinded readers are lint-clean by construction.

judged DV (no score, no rubric, no DV) — a bullet there would have sat behind a
trigger that structurally cannot fire at the moment of need, which is exactly the

(`.claude/rules/llm-judging.md`) is honored via the cross-pointer.

the audit), and `llm/api_dispatch.py` exposes no `betas` parameter (needed past a
200k window, ~298k input tokens for #1482's pair). The rule states the doctrine as
